text.p: Besides the non-recurring PSI acquisition expense, this year's third-quarter and nine-month losses also stem from write-offs of deferred offering costs, litigation expenses and other one-time write downs of inventory and other assets, as well as operating results for the currently reported quarter. This operating loss is only the second such loss in more than five years.

Excluding the effect of the LDA and PSI acquisitions, as well as the write-offs of deferred offering costs, litigation expenses and other one-time adjustments, IRIS would have had a net loss of approximately $612,000, or $0.10 per share, for the three months and $185,000, or $0.03 per share, for the nine months ended Sept. 30, 1996, compared with a net income of $564,000, or $0.09 per share, for three months and $1.2 million, or $0.18 per share, for nine months ended Sept. 30, 1995.

The 1996 third-quarter operating loss is primarily the result of a shortfall in sales of The Yellow IRIS; an almost $300,000 overrun on development of The White IRIS, the company's new white blood cell classifier; and $243,000 interest expense on its indebtedness incurred to acquire PSI.

IRIS also recently completed a review of its sale orders for the last 12 months in the light of a newly refined revenue recognition policy. As a result of the review, it has restated its results of operations for certain prior periods because the application of the refined policy to a number of sales transactions produced accounting results which, in retrospect, IRIS found inappropriate.

The transactions involved sales of several IVD imaging systems shipped "FOB destination" or, in three instances, subject to certain contingencies, as well as the redistribution of revenues for sales of the Model 900UDx under an introductory sales program. Restated results of operations compared with earlier reported results appear below and reflect the acquisition of StatSpin which was done in a "pooling-of-interests" transaction in February this year.
As Reported As Restated As Reported As Restated

Consequently, IRIS will amend its Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended Dec. 31, 1995, and its Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q for the three month periods ended March 31, 1996, and June 30, 1996, to reflect these adjustments. IRIS also has abandoned its earlier announced public offering and, instead, will seek other sources to refinance some of its newly assumed debt. Because of the events described, the company is not in compliance with two of the requirements of its loan with City National Bank and is holding discussions with the bank toward a work-out arrangement.

According to Fred Deindoerfer, IRIS chairman and chief executive officer: "IRIS is determined that these difficult events are put behind us quickly and resolute that the factors contributing to them do not re-occur. Our credibility with our many stockholders and the investment community at large, built over the last six years of growing profitability, must be restored as soon as possible."

As an important step in restoring profitability, IRIS implemented a previously announced restructuring that ultimately reduced its workforce by almost twenty percent. Most of the reductions occurred at the IRIS headquarters facility in Chatsworth. The restructuring is expected to reduce current expenditure levels by more than $1.9 million annually, after a one-time charge to earnings of approximately $300,000 in the fourth quarter for severance and other costs associated with the restructuring. Toward renewed profitability, sales of The Yellow IRIS in the first half of the fourth quarter already exceed those in the entire third quarter.
